everyone. Thank you for joining us. Our revenue growth for Q2 was 1.5% YoY and 1.2% sequentially
in constant currency terms. AI revenue was a standout at 10.5% of our revenue, growing at 29%
sequentially. And last quarter, it was at 8.2%.

and this is net new. This deal is expected to contribute over 1% revenue growth in the coming
financial year.
The second mega deal was for $1 bn for a renewal. Our large deal pipeline is healthy and includes
some other mega deals in this pipeline. Operating margin was stable at 21%. Free cash flow was
strong at $928 mn (Editor’s comment) for the quarter.
As enterprises adopt AI at scale, another quarter of strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of
our differentiated market positioning and client confidence. As an ecosystem integrator, we continue
to work closely with the frontier model companies, both open-weight and closed models. Our deep
investments in Topaz Fabric help our clients seamlessly navigate between models to ensure token
optimization and value realization.
Infosys continues to gain market share, especially where economics of the program is aligned to the
stakeholder interest. We remain the preferred AI strategy and deployment partner for our top clients.
As AI remains central to enterprise transformation in the years ahead, Infosys is well positioned to
help navigate this shift.
Based on our Q2 performance and revised outlook for rest of the year, our revenue growth guidance
is 1% to 2% YoY.in constant currency terms. Our operating margin guidance remains at 20% to 22%
for the year.
Thank you. And with that, we can open it up for questions.

Thank you very much. My first question is on your guidance. So, you have narrowed both the lower
and upper end. Could you help us understand why? Explain the margin performance, the benefit of
rupee depreciation, any offset and loss due to deflation, etc.? And did your salary hike also impact
your margins in the second half?
Third is, your AI revenue is 10.5% of your Q2 revenue. So how many deals won will have AI element?
And with AI jitters globally, is there a change in business? And fourth, how are your December quarter
furloughs shaping up versus last year and which sectors look the most vulnerable?
Salil Parekh
Okay. Let me start off with some of them, and Jayesh will also jump in with some of the other ones.
So first, AI is really an incredible performance for us. It is 10.5% of our revenue, growing sequentially
29%. We had laid out the AI approach in the Hexagon with six different areas of focus.
And in this revenue mix, we see each of those areas growing well, especially things that we do where
we are building agents, where we are doing legacy modernization, where we are doing process AI,
where we are doing data AI. So those are growing exceptionally well, but all of them are doing well.
And then we have the partner ecosystem with that. That is really gaining momentum.
I think in terms of the global AI our attention is really much more on the large enterprises with which
we are working. So for them, this is starting to become more-and-more relevant. And with the
investments we made and build the Topaz Fabric and the capabilities we have, plus all the training
that we have done for all of our people, which many and more are certified now, ready to do work
with different partners of the frontier companies, that is where we are getting the good traction with
the enterprise clients.
I will spend a couple of minutes on the industries. I think what we see, and Jayesh will add more to
that, we see really good strength on the Financial Services. We see good strength on Energy Utilities.
We see good strength on the Manufacturing. And we see some weakness on the Retail and we see
some weakness on the Hi-Tech. But it is a mix of all of those that we have put together in how we
see this.
Jayesh Sanghrajka
